cells.tense: The pen is in your hand and the room can see which thing you chose to watch.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you let go of to keep watching this, and say only that — no case, just the fact.
cells.core:
You decide what deserves your attention, and it shows in the open. What you keep your eyes on gets your time by not getting it spent elsewhere, and the people near you feel that without being told. Going well, this looks like watching closely, acting on what you find, and letting the next thing build from there.
What this clarity can feed next is what it already grows, tended rather than forced. Hold the shape of it while it builds. Care that doesn't exhaust is the whole trick. When people name what you've done, let that land on the work rather than on proof about you.
cells.sheetLine: You paid in attention for this, and the room can tell.
cells.verb: being seen for what you set aside to watch closely
cells.place: where you decide what deserves your attention

cells.tense: You're living a little ahead, in the version where the acknowledgment finally arrives and everything is settled.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you keep coming back to and act on it before you weigh it once more.
cells.core:
You're ahead of the moment you keep waiting for, running the version where it finally arrives. Weighing one thing against another is sharp, maybe sharper than the situation asks for, and each chance to do it again becomes the thing you do: this matters, no this, no this. All that comparing has its own price. It stands in for the watching instead of serving it, and the thing you can plainly see to do stops looking like the thing worth doing.
The way back is a practice that doesn't strain. One distinction, made and lived with. Not the flawless one — the one that lets you act. Comparing is a tool for watching closely, and it can't take the place of watching closely.

cells.tense: The door is behind you and you're parked at it, holding the same question about what to watch.
cells.ask: Notice one thing today, say it plainly to someone, and let the saying be the whole act.
cells.core:
Going well, this looks like looking at what's in front of you and acting on what you find, with nobody watching. Right now the watching has gone quiet. The door is behind you and you're parked at it — not moving on it, not naming it. What you can see hasn't gone anywhere.
What's starved isn't the ability to know what matters; it's the standing-while-knowing. Hold one thing in plain attention without forcing anything onto it. Put what you see in front of one person as observation, not proof. That doorway doesn't need returning to. Being here, noticing, is available now. Seeing comes back by being used.
cells.sheetLine: What you see hasn't gone anywhere. The watching stopped.

cells.tense: The pen is down and you're calling the handwriting on the page someone else's.
cells.ask: Name one thing you noticed this week and say, out loud, that it was yours to notice.
cells.core:
You walk into a room and you've sorted what matters before anyone speaks, then call it just walking in. Going well, this looks like choosing what counts and saying so plainly, so the people around you can build on it. Claiming it means owning that you did the sorting rather than letting the room take credit for it.
Pick one thing you've been passing off as obvious and say it's yours. Not loudly — just as the truth about who did the watching. What people do around your read already shows it. The claim is the part that's missing, and it's yours to make.
cells.sheetLine: You sort the room before anyone speaks. Say it was you.

attempts.check: The claim I can't fully support is that Honor here is about the person's own sacrifice being witnessed; the record says external acknowledgment of sacrifice generally, and the reader might say 'no one sacrificed anything — this is about my work being seen.' I read it as the sacrifice of attention: what Wisdom gives up to decide what matters. The ask survives being wrong because it's an act of attention, not an act of being honored — useful even if the person's sacrifice is something else. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line like 'you were never honored' — I cut that. Also cut any suggestion of what happened in the old room; Too Little only says the looking stopped, not where or when or who was there.
